q: Octopuses have three hearts.
a: Two hearts pump blood to the gills, while the third pumps it to the rest of the body.

q: Bananas are berries, but strawberries aren't.
a: Botanically, bananas qualify as berries, while strawberries are considered aggregate fruits.

q: Honey can last for thousands of years.
a: Properly sealed honey can remain edible for an incredibly long time because it has very little water and is naturally acidic.

q: A group of flamingos is called a flamboyance.
a: The wonderfully colorful name 'flamboyance' is used for a group of flamingos.

q: Cows have best friends.
a: Studies have found that cows can form strong social bonds and may become stressed when separated from preferred companions.

q: Butterflies taste with their feet.
a: Butterflies have taste receptors on their feet that help them identify plants.

q: A snail can have thousands of tiny teeth.
a: Some snail species have thousands of microscopic teeth arranged on a tongue-like structure called a radula.

q: Sharks are older than trees.
a: Shark ancestors existed hundreds of millions of years ago, before the first trees appeared on Earth.

q: Wombat poop is cube-shaped.
a: Wombats produce distinctive cube-shaped droppings, which helps keep the droppings from rolling away.

q: Sea otters sometimes hold hands while sleeping.
a: Sea otters may hold paws while resting so they don't drift apart from each other.

q: Crows can recognize human faces.
a: Crows are remarkably intelligent and can remember and recognize individual human faces.

q: Elephants can communicate using sounds humans cannot hear.
a: Elephants use very low-frequency sounds called infrasound that can travel long distances.

q: Some turtles can breathe through their butts.
a: Certain aquatic turtles can absorb oxygen through specialized tissues near their rear end while underwater.

q: A day on Venus is longer than a year on Venus.
a: Venus rotates so slowly that one rotation takes longer than the time it takes Venus to orbit the Sun.

q: There are volcanoes on Mars.
a: Mars is home to Olympus Mons, the largest known volcano in the Solar System.

q: Space is completely silent.
a: Sound needs a medium such as air or water to travel, and most of space is an extremely good vacuum.

q: A cloud can weigh hundreds of tons.
a: Although clouds look light and fluffy, a large cloud can contain an enormous amount of water.

q: Lightning can be hotter than the surface of the Sun.
a: The air in a lightning channel can reach temperatures of around 30,000 kelvin, several times hotter than the Sun's surface.

q: The Moon is slowly moving away from Earth.
a: The Moon drifts away from Earth by roughly 3.8 centimeters per year because of tidal interactions.

q: A day on Earth is very slightly getting longer.
a: Earth's rotation is gradually slowing, mainly because of tidal effects caused by the Moon.

q: There are more possible chess games than atoms in the observable universe.
a: The number of possible chess game variations is unimaginably huge, often estimated to exceed the number of atoms in the observable universe.

q: Your stomach gets a new lining regularly.
a: The stomach constantly replaces much of its protective lining because its digestive acids are extremely powerful.

q: Your brain uses a surprising amount of energy.
a: Although the brain makes up only a small percentage of body weight, it uses roughly 20 percent of the body's energy at rest.

q: Humans share a surprising amount of DNA with other living things.
a: Humans share many genes with organisms such as yeast because living things inherit biological instructions from ancient common ancestors.

q: Your fingerprints are unique.
a: The patterns on your fingertips develop before birth and are highly distinctive to each person.

q: Your nose can detect an incredible number of smells.
a: The human sense of smell can distinguish a huge variety of different odors using specialized receptors in the nose.

q: Some people sneeze when they look at bright light.
a: This is called the photic sneeze reflex, and it affects a noticeable portion of the population.

q: Goats have rectangular pupils.
a: A goat's horizontal, rectangular pupils give it a wide field of view that helps it watch for predators.

q: Goats can climb surprisingly steep places.
a: Mountain goats have specialized hooves that help them balance on rocky and steep surfaces.

q: Penguins propose with pebbles.
a: Some penguins use carefully selected pebbles during courtship and nest building.

q: Ravens can solve puzzles.
a: Ravens are highly intelligent birds capable of problem-solving, planning, and using objects as tools.

q: Dolphins have names for each other.
a: Dolphins develop unique signature whistles that can function somewhat like individual names.

q: Some frogs can freeze and survive.
a: Wood frogs can survive having much of their bodies frozen during winter and then become active again when temperatures rise.

q: A group of crows is called a murder.
a: One traditional collective noun for crows is a 'murder,' making it one of the more unusual animal group names.

q: Pineapples take a long time to grow.
a: Depending on the variety and growing conditions, a pineapple plant can take well over a year to produce a mature fruit.

q: Carrots were originally not usually orange.
a: Early cultivated carrots came in colors such as purple, yellow, white, and red before orange varieties became especially popular.

q: Apples float in water.
a: Apples are less dense than water because roughly a quarter of their volume can be air.

q: A pineapple is made from many flowers.
a: What looks like one pineapple fruit actually develops from many individual flowers that fuse together.

q: Avocados are fruits.
a: Despite being commonly used in savory dishes, avocados are botanically fruits and contain a large seed.

q: Chocolate was once used as money.
a: The ancient Maya and Aztecs valued cacao beans so highly that they were sometimes used in trade and as a form of currency.

q: The Eiffel Tower can change height.
a: Because metal expands when heated, the Eiffel Tower can become noticeably taller during hot weather.

q: Oxford University is older than the Aztec Empire.
a: Teaching existed at Oxford centuries before the Aztec Empire was established in the early 14th century.

q: Cleopatra lived closer to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid.
a: Cleopatra lived around 2,500 years after the Great Pyramid was built but only about 2,000 years before humans landed on the Moon.

q: The Great Wall of China is not one continuous wall.
a: It is actually a huge network of walls, fortifications, trenches, and other defensive structures built across different periods.

q: The Internet and the World Wide Web are not the same thing.
a: The Internet is the global network infrastructure, while the World Wide Web is a system of websites and webpages that operates on it.

q: The first computer mouse was made of wood.
a: The first computer mouse prototype, created by Douglas Engelbart's team, had a wooden casing.

q: A group of owls can be called a parliament.
a: 'Parliament' is one of the traditional collective nouns used for a group of owls.

q: Koalas have fingerprints.
a: Koalas have fingerprints that can look surprisingly similar to human fingerprints.

q: Jellyfish existed before dinosaurs.
a: Jellyfish-like animals have existed for hundreds of millions of years, long before dinosaurs appeared.

q: Some cats have extra toes.
a: Cats with extra toes are called polydactyl cats, and the extra digits can make their paws look unusually large.

q: A blue whale's heart is enormous.
a: A blue whale's heart is one of the largest hearts in the animal kingdom and can weigh hundreds of kilograms.

q: Sloths can hold their breath for a surprisingly long time.
a: Sloths can slow their heart rate and remain underwater for around 40 minutes or more.
